learningObjectives: Distinguish local XML data from a network API request.
Scan a local file and choose XML/JSON export.
Use XML resources and explicit persistence.
Inspect XML structure and affected TestStep references.

elements.text: API Scan File supports local message/definition files; the documented XSD workflow scans a schema and exports XML/JSON TestCases. Inspect whether your input is a data document or a schema; XML is hierarchical data, not inherently a relational database table.

Loading local XML does not by itself configure a network endpoint. Do not infer that every XML message must always fail or have an empty response: XML can also be used as a network API payload when transport is configured. A local file workflow and sending an HTTP request are different operations.

Open/Create XML file loads a file into a named resource. XML operations modify resources; Save XML file persists changes. Independent guidance: inspect the complete test, because a Save step can write to disk and resource-based editing is not a universal guarantee against data loss. Work with disposable copies and an explicit output path.

XML TestCases expose document, element, attribute, value, comment, declaration and CDATA control types. Insert adds new elements, Input changes existing ones and Verify checks values. Inspect generated structure and references rather than rely on an unverified universal Technical View absence claim.
Independent guidance: removing a Module element can affect its existing TestSteps. Inspect and synchronize affected references, then execute the relevant assertions.

Scan a disposable schema or file and inspect exported structure. Load a copy into a named resource and modify it without saving; separately test an explicit save to a disposable destination. Original Academy exercise files were inaccessible and no Tosca execution was performed.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing XML format and network transport
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming XML always means a local file with no response.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Determine whether the workflow is resource editing or a configured network message.

examPitfalls.title: Treating XML as a flat table
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect the XML control structure and intended element identity.

examPitfalls.title: Promising disk safety for every test
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Ignoring Save or other disk-writing steps.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use disposable files and explicit persistence review.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What follows from loading a local XML document alone?

options.text: A server always returns a response.
No network endpoint is configured merely by loading that file; transport must be configured separately for a request.
XML is automatically converted to REST.

practiceQuiz.rationale: XML data loading does not establish a service connection.

optionExplanations.A: A response needs an applicable network operation.
optionExplanations.B: This correctly separates local data and network configuration.
optionExplanations.C: Loading does not imply immediate persistence.
optionExplanations.D: XML format does not determine REST architecture.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which ActionMode changes an existing XML element?
practiceQuiz.rationale: The XML TestCase structure documents Input for modifying existing elements.

optionExplanations.C: Buffer is not the documented modification mode.
optionExplanations.D: Folder renaming is not XML element editing.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the persistence model for resource-based XML editing?

options.text: Changes affect the resource; an explicit Save step transfers changes to disk, so inspect that step.
Every run always creates a new source file.

practiceQuiz.hint: Resource manipulation and saving are distinct.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Resource-based edits require explicit persistence but do not prevent a configured Save from overwriting data.

optionExplanations.A: This states both the resource model and the persistence risk.
optionExplanations.B: Automatic read-only protection is not established.
optionExplanations.D: Automatic new-file creation is not guaranteed.

quickRecap.value: Distinguish a data document from an XSD schema.
XML/JSON TestCase is a documented file/schema export target.
XML format alone neither configures nor prohibits a server request.
Inspect hierarchy, namespaces and control types.
Modify resources; explicitly review disk persistence.
